newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Rogers to enter local telephone market.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Rogers to enter local telephone market.

text.p: Fresh from Thursday's decision by Canadian regulators to end the country's century-old local telephone service monopoly, Rogers Communications Inc. said on Friday it planned to enter the market.
Canada's largest cable operator and wireless telecommunications company said it would provide local telephone service to major urban areas it served in Ontario and British Columbia.

The Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission (CRTC) decided on Thursday to open up local telephone markets for competition. Local telephone service in Canada is now dominated by such companies as BCE Inc's Bell Canada telephone unit.
Rogers Chief Executive Ted Rogers said Rogers had a central office switch in Toronto capable of providing telephone service.

"Local telecommunications now represents vast opportunities for new products," said Rogers. "No company is better positioned than Rogers to undertake the local telecommunication opportunities now available in Canada."

Rogers Vice-President Phil Lind told shareholders that Rogers and the CRTC must work to resolve certain issues such as number portability, which would allow Rogers subscribers to keep their telephone numbers after switching to its service.
"Without number portability, the local telephone market is not truly open for competition," said Lind.
Eamon Hoey, an analyst at Hoey Associates, questioned whether Rogers' technology could be adapted to provide telephone service.
"It is a big leap," said Hoey.
Rogers executives also predicted that the money-losing company would enjoy solid growth earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amoritization (EBITDA) through the rest of 1997.
David Robinson, vice-president of inverstor relations, said the company expected one quarter in the next three years to show a net profit. He declined to specify which one.
CEO Rogers, 63, also told shareholders that he planned to retire within six years, after leading the company for 43 years.
Rogers Communications Inc. shares closed up C40 cents at C$8.10 on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Friday.
